assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: full; driver_capability: ready

## Reasoning

The scenario asserts a single user-observable invariant: one contiguous `working` span across a failing tool call and its correction inside ONE turn — `ready → working`, no flicker to `ready` or `waiting` between attempts, then `working → ready`. It is a lock on the parser's turn-boundary gate, not a feature test.

**agent_supports: yes.** GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.77 runs multiple shell tool calls within one turn and reacts to a failed one. Each invocation is a `tool.execution_start` / `tool.execution_complete` pair keyed on `data.toolCallId` in `$COPILOT_HOME/session-state/<session-id>/events.jsonl`; a FAILED execution presents as `data.success:false` on the completion, which `parseToolComplete` maps to `ParsedEvent.IsError` (parser.go:229-231). Several such pairs inside one turn, closed by a single `assistant.turn_end`, is exactly the shape this scenario needs. Under `--allow-all` (the driver's launch flag) both attempts auto-execute, so no retry cycle is interrupted by an approval gate.

**daemon_capability: full.** The no-flicker invariant holds STRUCTURALLY for this adapter rather than by timing luck, because copilot's turn boundary is explicit and the parser's dispatch is a closed switch (parser.go:85-119):

| observable | events.jsonl event | parser output | state effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| turn opens (`ready→working`) | `user.message` | `user_message` | → working |
| failing attempt | `tool.execution_start` + `tool.execution_complete` (`success:false`) | `function_call` + `function_call_output` with `IsError` | none — continued activity |
| the agent's between-attempts commentary | `assistant.message` | `assistant_message` | none — `parseAssistantMessage` deliberately never settles the turn (parser.go:187-188) |
| corrective attempt | second `tool.execution_start` / `tool.execution_complete` pair | `function_call` / `function_call_output` | none |
| turn ends (`working→ready`) | `assistant.turn_end` | `turn_done` | → ready |

Only `user.message` and `assistant.turn_end` move state; `waiting` is reachable ONLY via `permission_requested` (`permission.requested`), which `--allow-all` prevents. `session.start`, `assistant.turn_start`, model-change, usage-checkpoint, shutdown and subagent events are all `Skip=true`, and the `default` arm skips every event type a future CLI adds — so there is no bookkeeping line that could settle a mid-turn session to `ready`. Crucially, because the boundary is an explicit `assistant.turn_end` marker, the daemon runs NO idle/settle heuristic here: a long pause between the failing attempt and the recovery cannot be mistaken for turn completion, which is the failure mode this scenario exists to catch on heuristic adapters.

The `IsError` flag itself is timeline decoration, not a state input — asserting it is out of scope for a spec restricted to user-observable state.

Birth is the PRESESSION shape, not single-birth: copilot creates the session-state directory at launch but writes `events.jsonl` only when the first prompt is sent (driver SEAM 3), so `processlifecycle`'s scanner emits a transient `proc-<PID>` row first (scanner.go:347) and the real dir-keyed session id (`sessionIDFromPath`) arrives later. The spec models two birth phases and anchors every later phase to `session_birth`, templated from the mistral-vibe sibling for the same scenario. PID binding is by cwd (`DiscoverPIDByCWD("copilot", …)`, pid.go) against the `ExactName{copilot}` matcher.

**driver_capability: ready.** The recipe needs `send` / `wait_turn` / `sleep` only; all three are in `DRIVE_ELICITS` and genuinely ported. `wait_turn` counts `"type":"assistant.turn_end"` occurrences — an EXACT completed-turn count, so the driver does not return early between the failing and corrective attempts the way a tail-quietness heuristic could.

## Observations

`cost_nonzero` + `tokens_nonzero` are asserted and derivable OFFLINE from the staged transcript: output tokens land per `assistant.message.outputTokens` while the session runs, and both models this account can reach are priced in the committed replay capacity snapshot (`gpt-5-mini` directly; `claude-haiku-4-5` via the alias added for #1256).

`model` is deliberately NOT pinned: `--model` accepts only `auto` on this account and the router picks per turn between `gpt-5-mini` and `claude-haiku-4.5` (both seen in ONE live 1.0.77 session), so an exact match would fail on router choice rather than on a regression. `record` fills it from the recording.

## Recording override (2026-08-03)

RECORDING OVERRIDE (2026-08-03, recording 2026-08-03-12-43-26_irrlichd-0.5.9+bc0a957, 4/5): assessed daemon=full, the live recording refuted it. Copilot closes a turn after EVERY tool call and opens the continuation ~80 ms later: assistant.turn_end(turn 0) at 10:44:14.149Z, assistant.turn_start(turn 1) at 10:44:14.228Z, turn 1's assistant.message only 7.2 s later at 10:44:21.476Z. parser.go maps assistant.turn_end to turn_done (settles → ready) but lets assistant.turn_start fall to the default Skip arm, justified as "the open bracket of a turn the user message already put into working" — true for the first turn, false for a continuation turn, which has no preceding user.message. The daemon settled to `ready` at 12:44:16.383 (decided_by_rule agent_done) while the model was still generating, recovering only at 12:44:21.624 via "force ready→working on first activity" — a 5.24 SECOND false `ready` in the middle of the retry loop, before the correct final settle at 12:44:25.497. Same defect as sibling cell 2.2 auto-executed-tool-call, which showed it at only 122 ms because the tailer lagged; this recording shows the true magnitude. The birth is separately RE-ANCHORED: post-3cde4f8d the real session is born directly into `working`, which is the fix working as intended, not the bug. known_failing until the turn_start arm is fixed.

CORRECTION to the assess reasoning (does not change the state arc): copilot does NOT report a non-zero exit as a failed tool call. The `false` call produced tool.execution_complete with data.success TRUE; the failure appears only in data.result.content ("completed with exit code 1") and data.toolTelemetry.properties.shell_error_category ("command_nonzero_exit"). The parser's IsError path is therefore never reached by a shell failure, so the assess body's "data.success:false → IsError, NO state effect" chain is wrong in its premise and right in its conclusion.

RECIPE CORRECTION (committed separately as bc0a957d): wait_turn counts assistant.turn_end lines, which on copilot is NOT one per prompt — it returns at the FIRST turn_end, i.e. exactly the gap this cell exists to observe. The first staging run was truncated by it (wait_turn returned at turn_end(turn 0) 10:42:08.816Z, the 6 s tail expired before turn 1 closed at 10:42:14.923Z). Tail raised to 25 s; the assess claim that "the wait is exact and cannot return in the gap between the failing attempt and the recovery" is refuted.

## Fix confirmed (2026-08-03)

DAEMON=FULL RESTORED 2026-08-03 (re-recording 2026-08-03-17-53-34_irrlichd-0.5.9+ddbbdc1, 5/5). Commit 8df11518 ("fix(copilot): stop flashing `ready` mid-turn on a continuation turn") maps assistant.turn_start to a non-settling activity event instead of letting it fall to the default Skip arm, so a continuation turn opened after a tool call no longer reads as idle. The re-recording reproduces the provoking shape — the two bash calls (`false`, exit 1, and `echo recovered`, exit 0) complete at 15:54:21.795Z/15:54:21.883Z, assistant.turn_end(turn 0) lands 15:54:22.000Z and assistant.turn_start(turn 1) 49 ms later at 15:54:22.049Z with turn 1's assistant.message only at 15:54:23.953Z — and events.jsonl now carries exactly ONE working→ready transition (17:54:26.08, decided_by_rule agent_done, last_event_type turn_done) closing a single uninterrupted 43 s working span, with no ready→working rebound. The 5.24 s false `ready` the previous recording proved is gone; known_failing cleared, the original assess verdict daemon=full stands.
caveats: Whether copilot's bash tool reports a non-zero shell exit as `data.success:false` (→ `IsError`) or wraps it as a success with a non-zero exit code in `result` is NOT verified for 1.0.77 — kiro-cli does the latter. It does not affect this spec: neither shape produces a state transition, so the contiguous working span holds either way. The recipe's prompt asks for a command that fails AND for a retry, so the retry cycle happens regardless of how the failure is encoded.

The number of retry cycles is model-dependent. gpt-5-mini may run `false`, see it fail, and go straight to `echo recovered` (two tool calls), or interleave extra diagnostic calls. The spec asserts the SPAN, not a tool-call count, so a varying cycle count cannot fail it — but a run where the model refuses to execute a knowingly-failing command would produce a single tool call and should be re-driven with a sharper prompt, not accommodated by weakening the spec.

The no-waiting half of the invariant rests on the driver's `--allow-all` flag. Without it copilot raises `permission.requested`, the parser emits `permission_requested`, and the session correctly enters `waiting` — which is the sibling gated-tool scenario, not a failure of this one. If a recording flips to waiting here, tighten the launch flags rather than the spec.

`events.jsonl` does not exist until the first prompt is sent (driver SEAM 3, live-verified on 1.0.77), so the real session is born `ready` and moves to `working` within roughly the same second; the `session_birth` ready observation is tight and could be coalesced with `turn_start` by the tailer's debounce. If `record` sees it collapsed, re-anchor the phases rather than dropping the ready birth.

Input tokens are only reported at `session.shutdown` (a `session.usage_checkpoint` carries `totalNanoAiu` but NO token counts — verified live on 1.0.77). This recipe has no `exit_clean` step, so the recording carries output tokens only. That still satisfies tokens_nonzero/cost_nonzero, but the input half of the summary reads 0.

Recording spends real Copilot AI credits, and this cell is a MULTI-tool-call turn so it costs more than the single-call siblings. Export `COPILOT_AVAILABLE_TOOLS=bash` before driving (the driver forwards it as `--available-tools=bash`): tool definitions are ~8.3k of ~12k input tokens per turn, so restricting to the one tool this scenario needs roughly halves per-turn cost.

Same defect as sibling cell 2.2 auto-executed-tool-call, which showed it at only 122 ms because the tailer lagged; this recording shows the true magnitude. The birth is separately RE-ANCHORED: post-3cde4f8d the real session is born directly into `working`, which is the fix working as intended, not the bug. known_failing until the turn_start arm is fixed.

The `false` call produced tool.execution_complete with data.success TRUE; the failure appears only in data.result.content ("completed with exit code 1") and data.toolTelemetry.properties.shell_error_category ("command_nonzero_exit"). The parser's IsError path is therefore never reached by a shell failure, so the assess body's "data.success:false → IsError, NO state effect" chain is wrong in its premise and right in its conclusion.

The first staging run was truncated by it (wait_turn returned at turn_end(turn 0) 10:42:08.816Z, the 6 s tail expired before turn 1 closed at 10:42:14.923Z). Tail raised to 25 s; the assess claim that "the wait is exact and cannot return in the gap between the failing attempt and the recovery" is refuted.
Birth shape is now OBSERVED: the real session is born `working`, not `ready`; the proc-<PID> presession still carries the ready birth and remains the presession_birth anchor.

FIX CONFIRMED (supersedes the recording-proved daemon=bug caveat above): DAEMON=FULL RESTORED 2026-08-03 (re-recording 2026-08-03-17-53-34_irrlichd-0.5.9+ddbbdc1, 5/5). sources.note: ParseLine dispatch (85-119): only user.message and assistant.turn_end carry state; every other type incl. the default arm is Skip. parseToolComplete (224-232) maps data.success:false → IsError with NO state effect. parseAssistantMessage (183-208) documents that an assistant reply never settles the turn.
Source is FilesUnderRoot over ~/.copilot/session-state with sessionIDFromPath = the <session-id> directory (transcript basename is the constant events.jsonl); ExactName{copilot} matcher
DiscoverPIDByCWD("copilot", cwd, …) — cwd-only binding, no sidecar fallback; grounds the pid_bind phase
maybeTrackNewPID emits sessionID proc-<pid> (line 347) when no active transcript covers the PID, superseded once the real transcript appears — the presession two-phase birth this spec models

DRIVE_ELICITS (line 128) carries send/wait_turn/sleep; launch adds --allow-all (line 180) and honours COPILOT_AVAILABLE_TOOLS (line 181); wait_turn counts assistant.turn_end for an exact turn count so it cannot return between retry cycles; SEAM 3 records that events.jsonl appears only at the first prompt

live-captured 1.0.77 envelope fixtures: assistant.message.outputTokens is the live token signal; modelMetrics/currentTokens exist only on session.shutdown; both gpt-5-mini and claude-haiku-4.5 appear in one session
presession-shaped sibling spec for the SAME scenario (FilesUnderRoot + dir-keyed session id) — the two-phase birth + intermediate_working shape templated here
copilot sibling establishing the presession birth, --allow-all no-waiting invariant and the unpinned-model observation policy this cell reuses

preconditions: copilot CLI 1.0.77 on PATH and authenticated (credentials live in the OS keychain, so COPILOT_HOME isolation needs no re-login)
An active Copilot plan with AI credits — this recording spends them, and a multi-tool-call turn costs more than the single-call siblings
irrlichd is recording (run-cell.sh isolated mode, or --attach against a --record daemon)
tmux available (the interactive driver drives the REPL through it)
setup: The driver isolates state under $STAGING/copilot-home via COPILOT_HOME (the supported lever; --config-dir is deprecated) and seeds trustedFolders + askedSetupTerminals so neither first-run prompt blocks the input box

Launch is `copilot --allow-all --no-color` in a fresh per-run cwd under <staging>/cwd/, so BOTH the failing and the corrective bash call auto-execute and no permission.requested is ever written — that is what makes the no-waiting half of the invariant structural rather than incidental

Recommended: export COPILOT_AVAILABLE_TOOLS=bash before driving. The driver forwards it as --available-tools=bash, which drops the unused tool definitions (~8.3k of ~12k input tokens) and roughly halves the credits this cell costs
Interactive, not headless: the REPL must outlive the turn so the daemon observes the working→ready settle rather than a process exit

wait_turn counts assistant.turn_end lines, and on copilot that is NOT one per prompt: the CLI closes a turn after every tool call and opens the continuation ~50 ms later, so wait_turn returns at the FIRST turn_end — precisely in the gap between the failing attempt and the recovery. The 2026-08-03 recording proved it (wait_turn returned at turn_end(turn 0) 10:42:08.816Z while turn 1 ran to 10:42:14.923Z). The trailing sleep is therefore 25 s, not 6 s: it must outlast the whole retry loop, because wait_turn cannot.

script.text: Using the bash tool, run the shell command `false` — it will fail. Then, in this same turn, retry with the bash tool running `echo recovered`. Then reply with just: done

verify: events.jsonl shows a transient proc-<PID> presession born ready, then the real <session-id> session (a DIFFERENT id, the session-state directory name) born ready when the transcript appears
events.jsonl shows exactly one ready→working transition for the real session
at least 2 tool_use events for the bash tool fall inside that working span (tool.execution_start / tool.execution_complete pairs on distinct toolCallIds — the failing attempt and the recovery)
events.jsonl contains NO state_transition to ready between the failing tool result and the corrective tool call
events.jsonl contains NO state_transition to waiting at any point during the working span (--allow-all → no permission.requested)
events.jsonl shows exactly one working→ready transition, at the assistant.turn_end that closes the turn
the newest recording's replay summary shows cum_output_tokens > 0 and estimated_cost_usd > 0, with model_name one of gpt-5-mini / claude-haiku-4.5 (router's choice — not pinned)
